newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco court case against Mass. postponed.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco court case against Mass. postponed.

text.p: A federal court hearing set for Tuesday on a legal challenge to a Massachusetts law that would force tobacco companies to disclose their ingredients has been postponed, the state attorney general's office said Monday.
No new date has been set for the case, a spokeswoman said.

Four tobacco companies -- Philip Morris Cos. Inc., R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp. and Lorillard Tobacco Co. -- have challenged the law, which is scheduled to take effect in July 1997.

The companies contend the law, which would be the first in the nation to force tobacco companies to reveal their ingredients, would reveal their trade secrets and would pre-empt federal laws on tobacco.
The legislation, signed into law last August, would also set tougher tests to measure the nicotine intake from cigarettes, snuff and chewing tobacco.

If the law passes the legal challenge, it could spur other states to pass similar laws and force the tobacco companies to change their ingredients, the measure's sponsor, state Sen. Warren Tolman, has said.

Legislators and health officials in Illinois, Florida, New York, Texas, Minnesota, Michigan and other states have contacted Massachusetts officials about the law, Tolman and other officials have said.
The tobacco companies said in court papers they might stop selling tobacco in Massachusetts, where annual sales top $1.2 billion, if the law went into effect.
R.J. Reynolds is part of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp., Brown & Williamson is a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc and Lorillard is part of Loews Corp.
